parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the resistance of a power supply. The circuit has been set up for you. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Connect the crocodile clip near end X of the resistance wire. • Switch on. • Adjust the position of the crocodile clip until the potential difference V across terminals P and Q is 2.0 V. • Record, in Table 1.1, the value of the current I shown on the ammeter. • Move the crocodile clip and record values of I for V = 1.8 V, 1.6 V, 1.4 V and 1.2 V. • Switch off. Table 1.1 I / A V / V 2.0 1.8 1.6 1.4 1.2 [2]

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text:
5 I values, all increasing
all < 5.00 A and to 2dp at least

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of V / V ( y -axis) against I / A ( x -axis). [4]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
graph:
axes labelled with quantity and unit
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
plots all correct to ½ small square
Well-judged straight line and thin line, precise plots

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Determine the gradient M of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. M = .......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 1(c)(i)
ms.text: M present and triangle method seen on graph

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The gradient M is numerically equal to the resistance R of the power supply. Write down the resistance R to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. R = .......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(c)(ii)
ms.text:
R in range 0.5 to 4.0 Ω
2 or 3 sig figs and unit = Ω

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
suitable reason:
e.g.:
wire becomes too hot,
current exceeds full scale deflection(owtte) of meter/becomes too large

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) In this type of experiment, it is possible to change the potential difference by using a variable resistor rather than using different lengths of a resistance wire. In the space, draw the standard circuit symbol for a variable resistor. [1]
